title: Adaptive ring scheduler for heterogeneous batching with priority KV prefetch
author: Priya Sharma
description: Motivation: production workloads show wide variance in sequence lengths and per-request priorities; static ring scheduling leaves high-priority short requests waiting behind long-running shards, and KV-cache prefetches for upcoming tokens are not coordinated with cross-GPU NIC timelines. This PR introduces an adaptive ring scheduler that dynamically reorders tensor-parallel collectives to maximize overlap of communication and compute across heterogeneous micro-batches and integrates a priority-aware KV prefetch queue to reduce tail latency. Summary of changes: 1) scheduler/adaptive_ring_scheduler: new C++ core that monitors per-peer bandwidth/latency, outstanding micro-batch sizes, and request priority tags and emits an ordered sequence of collective operations that maximizes comm/compute overlap; 2) comm/nccl_tuning: add prioritized stream allocation and backlog-aware concurrency limits exposed as runtime knobs; 3) kv/prefetcher: implement priority prefetch queue with soft-deadline semantics and early-retry on slower peers; 4) kernels/allreduce_fused.cu: introduce an optional fused allreduce+scale kernel used when the scheduler selects aggregation-first ordering to reduce PCIe hops; 5) batching/hetero_packing: smarter micro-batch packing to reduce padding when pairing long and short sequences; 6) tracing/metrics: new metrics for prefetch hit rate, scheduler reorder rate, and per-request overlap efficiency; 7) tests/perf: new benchmark harness that reproduces mixed-length, mixed-priority workloads. Backwards compatibility: defaults maintain previous ordering unless admin enables adaptive scheduler in runtime config (runtime.config.enable_adaptive_scheduler=true). Checklist: - [x] design doc and perf plan (docs/design/adaptive_ring.md) - [x] unit tests for scheduler decision logic - [x] integration tests against NCCL multi-node CI - [x] benchmarks measuring 99th percentile latency improvements - [x] feature flag gating for gradual rollout Performance results: on our internal 8xA100 cluster with mixed-length synthetic traffic (50% short 64 tokens, 50% long 2048 tokens) and a 30% high-priority request subset, we measured: - 95th p99 latency reduced from 48ms to 30ms for high-priority requests (37% improvement) - aggregate token throughput improved 12% due to reduced wasted padding and better overlap - KV prefetch hit rate improved from 67% to 89% for prioritized requests Risk and mitigations: scheduler makes heuristic decisions that could cause starvation of low-priority work under extreme load; mitigated by a tunable fairness window and a cap on priority reorders (runtime knobs added). The fused kernel is optional and guarded by a runtime capability check. Deployment plan: behind feature flag and gated per-customer; rollout to dedicated clusters with canary traffic, monitor prefetch hit rate and p99 latency, and enable auto-fallback to legacy ring ordering on regression. Related: ENG-4897 (scheduler roadmap), ENG-4912 (KV cache improvements), SUP-2101 (customer incident that triggered this work).
commits: feat(scheduler): add adaptive ring scheduling core loop and basic heuristics
perf(kv): add priority prefetch queue and metrics
chore(nccl): expose prioritized streams and concurrency knobs
perf(kernels): optional fused allreduce+scale kernel with unit tests
test(ci): add multi-node hetero-batching perf job
discussion: Evan Park: Nice design. Question: how do you prevent priority inversion when many high-priority short requests stream in?
Priya Sharma: We cap reorders per fairness window; default window is 100ms and cap=4 reorders per window. Added config knobs and unit tests for starvation scenarios.
Lina Gomez: Can the fused kernel be toggled at runtime? What about driver compatibility?
Priya Sharma: Yes behind runtime capability check and a flag runtime.kernels.enable_fused_allreduce; the build includes a fallback; added a CI matrix job for driver combinations.
Marcus Chen: CI showed flakiness on one NCCL test in the first run; reran and added a retry/backoff in the test harness. Verified stability in subsequent runs.
release_notes: Add adaptive ring scheduler with prioritized KV prefetching and optional fused allreduce kernel. Improves p99 latency for prioritized short requests in mixed workloads and increases overall throughput by reducing padding and improving comm/compute overlap. Feature is disabled by default and gated by runtime config.
